Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; to understand what is causing this, how long has it been present and is it itchy or painful?

REQUEST TEST: Skin_Culture

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Seborrheic Dermatitis

Your mention of the rash worsening in cold weather and the presence of greasy yellow scales is very characteristic of this condition, which often affects the scalp and forehead. I have already requested a skin culture to rule out secondary infection; can you tell me if you have a history of similar flares or if you have any known allergies?
